faq_add.q: Can a Nepali student work part time in Georgia or Kazakhstan?
faq_add.a: Georgia changed its rules on 1 March 2026: a foreign national who is not a permanent resident now needs a separate "right to work" before any paid or self employed work, and international students are not on the exemption list (inc.ge, jam-news.net, studyu.org). The employer applies for it, so a cafe job is no longer informal. Kazakhstan is stricter: the International Educational Corporation, Almaty Management University and Abai Kazakh National Pedagogical University all say a student visa holder may not work, and the Abai page calls it an administrative offence. Older agency pages that promise 20 hours a week in either country are not backed by these sources, so budget your whole fee and living cost without wages. Ask your university in writing before you accept any job.

faq_add.q: How much does the Nepal government spend on scholarships, and who gets the money?
faq_add.a: The Ministry of Education, Science and Technology said on 9 February 2025 that it had set aside NPR 7.39 billion for scholarships in 2081/82, for about 1.5 million students from primary to higher and technical education (OnlineKhabar and Edusanjal). The biggest lines: NPR 5.11 billion for 10,594 students in medical education, NPR 603.2 million for 12,065 students on residential scholarships (NPR 50,000 a year each), NPR 210 million for 552,000 Dalit students in Class 1 to 5, NPR 600 million for economically disadvantaged students (NPR 24,000 a year in Class 11 and 12 science, NPR 18,000 in other subjects, NPR 6,000 in Class 6 to 10) and NPR 59.4 million for technical education. Karnali girls in Class 1 to 5 get NPR 1,000 a year. Ask your school or local level which list your name can be put on, because most of these do not have a national online form.

faq_add.q: I am Dalit, Muslim or from a marginalised family: what does a CTEVT diploma cost me?
faq_add.a: Nothing, if you get a seat in the special scholarship. The ministry says Dalit, Muslim and marginalised students in technical education get a monthly stipend of NPR 3,500, a yearly travel allowance of NPR 1,500 and a clothing allowance (NPR 2,000 on one page, NPR 2,500 on another); the CTEVT special scholarship notice also lists free hostel accommodation. CTEVT announced 480 seats for 2083 (457 diploma and 23 pre diploma) for these groups and for 78 local levels where technical education had not reached. For the 3,417 classified (free) seats, half go to the general group and half to targeted groups. A student who got a CTEVT scholarship once cannot get another, and must serve where the government assigns after finishing if it asks.

faq_add.q: Can I study medicine in English in Bulgaria, and what does it cost?
faq_add.a: Yes, in Sofia, Plovdiv, Varna and Pleven. A 2026/27 guide (studyu.org) lists EUR 8,000 a year at Sofia University Faculty of Medicine, EUR 9,950 at the Medical University of Sofia and EUR 10,000 at Plovdiv, so six years cost about EUR 48,000 to 60,000 (roughly NPR 84 lakh to 1.05 crore at EUR 1 about NPR 175). Two older guides print EUR 7,000 to 8,000, so read each university's own page. Selection is an entrance exam in biology and chemistry (Sofia holds one remote exam for non EU applicants in September). The European Commission says a student may work 20 hours a week without a work permit. Before you pay, ask the Nepal Medical Council whether it recognises that exact university, because you must pass the NMC licensing examination after returning; NEET is an Indian test and does not apply to you.

faq_add.q: How long can I stay in Bulgaria or Croatia after graduating to look for a job?
faq_add.a: The European Commission EU Immigration Portal says that in Bulgaria you can look for and start work within 9 months after finishing if you register with the Employment Agency within 7 business days, and then you need a work permit on the same terms as other non EU citizens. For Croatia it says you can stay for one year, renewable for one more year, to look for work or set up a business. During study both countries allow 20 hours of work a week (Croatia outside study time; Bulgaria also in holidays). Rules change, so check the Ministry of Interior before you plan.

faq_add.q: Is Luxembourg really almost free for a Nepali student?
faq_add.a: Tuition is, living is not. The University of Luxembourg is the only public university and lists enrolment fees of EUR 400 a semester for the first two bachelor semesters, EUR 200 a semester afterwards and generally EUR 200 a semester for a master (about NPR 70,000 to 1.4 lakh a year at EUR 1 about NPR 175). One 2024 guide prints EUR 400 to 800 a semester for non EU students, so read the programme page. Guides quote proof of funds of EUR 950 a month excluding rent, up to EUR 1,100 to 1,500 a month, and the university is quoted at about EUR 1,500 a month, which is NPR 20 to 31 lakh a year. The European Commission says master and PhD students may work 15 hours a week in term time (bachelor students only after two semesters) and 40 hours a week in holidays, and that graduates may stay to look for a job or start a business.

faq_add.q: Can I stay and work in Greece after studying there?
faq_add.a: Not directly. The European Commission EU Immigration Portal says that in Greece you can work part time during studies, you cannot change your status to a residence permit for another purpose, and after completing your studies you must return to your home country and submit a fresh application from there. Compare this with Bulgaria (9 months), Croatia (1 year, renewable once) and Luxembourg (stay to look for a job or start a business) before choosing. Two 2026 guides (unipage.net, eecglobal.com) say a newer Greek law (5275/2026) gives a one year post study permit to look for work, which the Commission page does not show, so confirm with the Ministry of Migration and Asylum before you rely on either. Greek taught public bachelor programmes are free for non EU students too, but need Greek at B2.

faq_add.q: What does Slovenia cost for a student from outside the EU?
faq_add.a: For 2026/27 a bachelor year at a public university mostly costs EUR 2,100 to 5,880 and a master year EUR 2,505 to 6,800 (studyu.org), for example EUR 3,400 and EUR 4,700 at the University of Ljubljana School of Economics and Business. The University of Ljubljana recommends at least EUR 700 a month for living and the residence permit needs proof of at least EUR 507.43 for each month of study; a dormitory bed averages about EUR 197 a month in Ljubljana. Most bachelor programmes are taught in Slovenian, with English mainly at master and doctoral level. On the European Commission page, a student permit holder may work under the Acts on employment relationships and student work, and to stay after studying your employer starts the employment permit application.

faq_add.q: Is the Darmasiswa scholarship a degree, and can a Nepali student apply?
faq_add.a: Darmasiswa is a one year non degree programme of Indonesia's Ministry of Primary and Secondary Education to study Bahasa Indonesia, arts, music, dance or crafts at about 60 universities. The official site says it is for students from countries that have diplomatic relations with Indonesia and that more than 111 countries have taken part since 1976. The host university UNY lists the rules as unmarried, aged 18 to 32, with a high school diploma or equivalent, and says it returned in 2026 after pausing in 2024. One third party listing prints a monthly allowance of IDR 4,700,000 and a 15 May to 15 June 2026 window; the 2026 amounts were still to be announced on the UNY page, so confirm on darmasiswa.kemendikdasmen.go.id. It will not give you a bachelor or master; for a degree look at the KNB scholarship instead.

faq_add.q: Is the Vietnam Government Scholarship open to Nepal, and the Iceland one?
faq_add.a: Vietnam: the official application portal studyinvietnam.edu.vn lists Nepal in its country menu, so a Nepali applicant can open an application for a bachelor, master or doctorate. Quotas, subjects and any nomination step follow the agreement and change every year, so no seat count is given here, and many places are for programmes taught in Vietnamese. Iceland: the Icelandic Government scholarship for the BA in Icelandic as a Second Language names the citizens it is open to (Austria, Canada, China, Germany, Norway, Poland, Slovakia, the United Kingdom, the United States through Fulbright and others) and Nepal was not among them in the 2026 call text, so it is not a route for a Nepali student.

faq_add.q: Which scholarships fund a Nepali student for a master or PhD in Saudi Arabia or Armenia?
faq_add.a: KAUST in Saudi Arabia gives its fellowship to every admitted MS and PhD student of any nationality: tuition and bench fees, a stipend of about USD 20,000 a year for MS and USD 25,000 to 30,000 for PhD, housing and insurance (guides value it at USD 70,000 to 80,000 a year). Listings want a STEM degree, a GPA of about 3.0 of 4 and TOEFL iBT 81 or IELTS 6.5; one guide prints a 3 January 2027 deadline for Fall 2027, so read the KAUST portal. In Armenia the American University of Armenia says international students are eligible for merit scholarships of up to 50 percent of tuition through a separate International Scholarship application to its Office of Financial Aid; need based aid up to 90 percent is for Armenian citizens only.

ge.work: Not as a student without a separate permit. Since 1 March 2026 any foreign national who is not a permanent resident needs a "right to work" from the Georgian authorities before any paid or self employed work, including remote work for a Georgian employer, and international students are not on the exemption list (inc.ge, jam-news.net and studyu.org, 2026). One legal commentary says a student who already holds a valid residence card does not need a separate work visa but still needs the right to work, and the employer files the application. Earlier agency claims of 20 hours a week are out of date; do not budget for income.

kz.work: Not allowed on the student visa. Three university pages say it: the International Educational Corporation (foreign students are not allowed to work), Almaty Management University (not eligible to work) and Abai Kazakh National Pedagogical University (carrying out labor activities with a student visa is an administrative offence). Older agency pages that say 20 hours a week are not backed by a university or official page, so plan to pay for your studies without wages.

abroad_note_add.is: The Icelandic Government scholarship for the BA in Icelandic as a Second Language lists the citizens it is open to (Austria, Canada, China, Germany, Norway, Poland, Slovakia, the United Kingdom, the United States through Fulbright and others) and Nepal is not among them in the 2026 call text, so it is not a route for Nepali students (the-updates.com, european-funding-guide.eu).
abroad_note_add.am: The American University of Armenia teaches in English and lists international undergraduate tuition of AMD 3,700,000 (most programmes) to 4,250,000 (BA in Business) a year on its own tuition page, with merit scholarships of up to 50 percent (admissions.aua.am).
abroad_note_add.ge: Government Resolution No. 437 of 8 September 2026 sets how state universities admit international students (the rector consents within the places the government approves for each programme and year), and a university must suspend a foreign student who earns no more than one third of the year's credits; if 90 days pass after the suspension the Public Service Development Agency may end the study residence permit (studyu.org, 30 September 2026).

vn: so no Nepal specific call was confirmed
and the official application portal (studyinvietnam.edu.vn) lists Nepal in its country menu, but no Nepal specific call or quota was confirmed

fw14-4: Georgia: unclear, guides say 20 hours but others say jobs are informal.
Georgia: not without a separate right to work since 1 March 2026 (inc.ge, jam-news.net).

scholarships_add.name: Darmasiswa Indonesian Scholarship (Bahasa Indonesia, arts and culture, one year, non-degree)
scholarships_add.by: Ministry of Primary and Secondary Education of Indonesia with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs
scholarships_add.covers: Tuition at the host university, a monthly living allowance (IDR 4,700,000 in one third party listing; the host university UNY said the 2026 amounts were still to be announced) and a book allowance. Airfare and the visa fee are paid by you. It is a one year course, not a degree.
scholarships_add.who: Young people from countries that have diplomatic relations with Indonesia (the official site says more than 111 countries have taken part since 1976): unmarried, aged 18 to 32 and holding a high school diploma or equivalent (UNY page), who choose Bahasa Indonesia or an arts, music, dance or craft subject at one of about 60 host universities. No earlier Indonesian is needed.
scholarships_add.how: Register online on the official Darmasiswa site (darmasiswa.kemendikdasmen.go.id) and pick host universities. The programme paused after 2024 and returned for 2026; one third party page reports a 15 May to 15 June 2026 window, so expect a similar window in 2027 and read the dates on the official site.

scholarships_add.name: Vietnam Government Scholarship (VIED, Ministry of Education and Training)
scholarships_add.by: Vietnam International Education Development (VIED), Ministry of Education and Training of Vietnam
scholarships_add.covers: Tuition and a monthly living allowance; the exact amounts and subjects follow the bilateral agreement and level (guides print USD 700 to 800 a month, which no official page confirms). Many places are for programmes in Vietnamese with a language year first.
scholarships_add.who: Nationals of countries with an education agreement with Vietnam. The official application portal (studyinvietnam.edu.vn) lists Nepal in its country menu, so a Nepali applicant can open an application; other pages say some countries are nominated by their own ministry first and quotas are yearly, so no fixed Nepal quota is confirmed here.
scholarships_add.how: Create an account on studyinvietnam.edu.vn, choose level, university and subject and upload your documents. Guides place the nomination window in the first half of the year for a September or October start; the dates change every year, so check the portal.

scholarships_add.name: American University of Armenia merit scholarship for international students
scholarships_add.covers: A merit based reduction of up to 50 percent of tuition for international students. The AUA tuition table for international students shows AMD 4,250,000 a year for the BA in Business and AMD 3,700,000 for other undergraduate programmes (about NPR 14 to 16 lakh at AMD 1 about NPR 0.38); a 2026/27 guide prints USD 11,700 to 13,080, so read the current table before you plan.
scholarships_add.who: International applicants (not citizens of Armenia, ethnic Armenians or Armenian special passport holders, who get an automatic AMD 2,000,000 subsidy and need based aid up to 90 percent) who apply to an AUA bachelor or master programme taught in English.
scholarships_add.how: Apply for admission and send the separate Application for International Scholarship to the AUA Office of Financial Aid by its deadline; AUA asks you to send it as early as possible, alongside the admission application.

scholarships_add.name: KAUST Fellowship (King Abdullah University of Science and Technology)
scholarships_add.by: King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST), Thuwal, Saudi Arabia
scholarships_add.covers: Admission and funding come together: tuition and bench fees, a stipend of about USD 20,000 a year for MS and USD 25,000 to 30,000 for PhD, on campus housing, health and dental insurance and relocation (guides value the package at USD 70,000 to 80,000 a year).
scholarships_add.who: Applicants of any nationality with a relevant STEM bachelor (MS) or master (PhD), a GPA of about 3.0 of 4 or better (listings say 3.5 is competitive) and English proof such as TOEFL iBT 81 or IELTS 6.5. There is no application fee and GRE is optional (listings).
scholarships_add.how: Apply online on the KAUST admissions portal for the August intake. One guide (November 2026) prints a 3 January 2027 deadline for Fall 2027 while older listings show 17 January and 11 April for 2026, so read the portal for the exact date.

scholarships_add.name: Ministry of Education scholarship for economically disadvantaged students (Class 11 and 12 and technical)
scholarships_add.by: Ministry of Education, Science and Technology (MoEST), Government of Nepal
scholarships_add.covers: In 2081/82 the ministry set aside NPR 600 million for economically disadvantaged students: NPR 24,000 a year for Class 11 and 12 science, NPR 18,000 a year for other Class 11 and 12 subjects and NPR 6,000 a year for Class 6 to 10 (both news pages). For technical education the same news pages print NPR 15,000 a year for general courses and NPR 21,000 a year for technical courses.
scholarships_add.who: Students from economically disadvantaged families who study in a community school or approved institution; the school or local level confirms the family situation. The ministry did not print a student count for this scheme in the pages read.
scholarships_add.how: Ask the school principal or your local level education unit about the yearly list and documents; the ministry publishes quotas through the local level, not through a single national form.

scholarships_add.name: Ministry of Education technical education scholarship for Dalit, Muslim and marginalised students
scholarships_add.by: Ministry of Education, Science and Technology (MoEST), delivered through CTEVT
scholarships_add.covers: A budget of NPR 59.4 million in 2081/82 pays a monthly stipend of NPR 3,500, a yearly travel allowance of NPR 1,500 and a yearly clothing allowance (NPR 2,000 on Edusanjal, NPR 2,500 on OnlineKhabar and in the CTEVT special scholarship 2082 notice). The CTEVT notice adds free hostel accommodation.
scholarships_add.who: Students from Dalit, Muslim, disadvantaged and marginalised communities who qualify for a CTEVT diploma or pre diploma seat. The CTEVT special scholarship (480 seats for 2083, with 78 local levels without access to technical education) is the main way seats are given.
scholarships_add.how: Apply on the yearly CTEVT special scholarship notice (see the CTEVT special scholarship in this list); the stipend rates above are the ministry figures for that scheme.

scholarships_add.name: Ministry of Education higher education scholarship for martyr, conflict victim, Kamalari, Muslim women and disabled students
scholarships_add.by: Ministry of Education, Science and Technology (MoEST), Government of Nepal
scholarships_add.covers: NPR 24,000 a year at bachelor and master level (Edusanjal, 9 February 2025, quoting the ministry for 2081/82).
scholarships_add.who: Children of martyrs, conflict victims, freed Kamalari, Muslim women and students with disabilities who study at bachelor or master level. A separate residential scheme pays NPR 50,000 a year to students with disabilities, freed Kamlari, marginalised students, street children, HIV affected students and Badi community students (12,065 students, NPR 603.2 million, OnlineKhabar).
scholarships_add.how: Apply through your campus or the university scholarship notice that follows the ministry call; keep the proof of category (martyr or conflict victim certificate, disability card or local level letter).

exams: Medicine, dentistry and pharmacy in English: an entrance exam in biology and chemistry (Medical University of Sofia holds one remote exam for non EU applicants in September; Plovdiv runs online tests from April to August plus a September resit)
English proof or an interview for English taught programmes
A Bulgarian language preparatory year (about EUR 3,500 at Sofia University) if you study in Bulgarian
abroad_add.intakes: October (the academic year starts on 1 October; non EU applications at Sofia University ran 27 July to 11 September for 2026/27)
abroad_add.work: You can work without a work permit for 20 hours a week during the academic year and during official holidays (European Commission EU Immigration Portal, Bulgaria page).
abroad_add.stay_back: Within 9 months after finishing you may look for and start work if you register with the Employment Agency within 7 business days; you then need a work permit on the same terms as other non EU citizens (European Commission EU Immigration Portal).
abroad_add.note: Mostly chosen for English medium medicine: 2026/27 non EU fees are EUR 8,000 a year at Sofia University Faculty of Medicine, EUR 9,950 at the Medical University of Sofia and EUR 10,000 at Plovdiv (studyu.org), while two older guides print EUR 7,000 to 8,000 and a Pleven fee of about EUR 9,000, so read the university's own 2026/27 page; six years cost about EUR 48,000 to 60,000 at those rates. Non medical bachelor programmes at public universities start near EUR 3,300 a year (Sofia University, 2026/27). Living is quoted at EUR 500 to 900 a month by the European Commission and EUR 500 to 850 at Sofia; a dormitory is about EUR 100 a month and the residence permit is for one year and renewable, tied to your programme. A foreign MD counts for a licence in Nepal only if the Nepal Medical Council recognises that exact university, and you must pass the NMC licensing examination after returning, so ask the council before you pay a deposit. NEET is an Indian test and does not apply to Nepali applicants. NPR figures are rough, at EUR 1 about NPR 175.

exams: Program specific entrance test (Biology and Chemistry for medicine)
English proof for English taught programmes, usually IELTS 6.0 or TOEFL iBT 80 and above (one guide)
Croatian language year for Croatian taught programmes
abroad_add.intakes: October (winter semester); non EU applications run roughly February or March to May, June or July depending on the faculty (one guide: University of Zagreb 1 February to 31 May)
abroad_add.work: Outside study time you may be employed or run a self employed activity for up to 20 hours a week (European Commission EU Immigration Portal, Croatia page).
abroad_add.stay_back: After completing studies you can stay for one year, renewable for one more year, to look for work or set up a business (European Commission EU Immigration Portal).
abroad_add.note: English taught general programmes at public universities cost about EUR 1,100 to 4,500 a year (Europe Study, CounsellorMaster, another guide EUR 4,500 to 10,000), while the University of Zagreb School of Medicine in English lists EUR 12,000 a year for 2026/27 with 60 places (medschool-experts.com; a second guide prints EUR 9,000 to 11,000, so read the faculty page), dentistry EUR 5,100 a semester and veterinary EUR 5,500 a semester. Croatian taught programmes are free after a Croatian language year (one guide). Living is quoted at EUR 400 to 800 a month, EUR 700 to 1,000 for medicine in Zagreb. The temporary stay permit is for one year or the length of the programme if shorter and you ask for the extension at least 60 days before it expires (European Commission). A foreign MD counts for a licence in Nepal only if the Nepal Medical Council recognises that exact university, and you must pass the NMC licensing examination after returning, so ask the council before you pay a deposit. NEET is an Indian test and does not apply to Nepali applicants. NPR figures are rough, at EUR 1 about NPR 175.

exams: B2 English (TOEFL, IELTS, PTE or the faculty's own test) for English taught programmes
Slovenian B2 for programmes in Slovenian (the Ljubljana medicine faculty sets its own exam)
Entrance test or document review set by each faculty
abroad_add.intakes: October (academic year starts 1 October; winter semester October to January, summer semester February to mid July)
fields: Humanities and social science (English mostly at master and doctoral level)
abroad_add.work: A holder of a temporary residence permit for study may take up employment or work in Slovenia during the permit under the Acts on employment relationships and student work (European Commission EU Immigration Portal, Slovenia page).
abroad_add.stay_back: If you want to work after studying, your future employer starts an application for an employment permit and you apply for a further temporary residence permit; applying from inside Slovenia is possible (European Commission).
abroad_add.note: For a non EU citizen a bachelor year at a public university in 2026/27 mostly costs EUR 2,100 to 5,880 and a master year EUR 2,505 to 6,800 (studyu.org), for example EUR 3,400 and EUR 4,700 at the University of Ljubljana School of Economics and Business plus a EUR 61.60 annual contribution; free places go to EU citizens and a few other groups. Most bachelor programmes are taught in Slovenian and English concentrates at master and doctoral level. The University of Ljubljana recommends at least EUR 700 a month on top of tuition, the residence permit needs proof of at least EUR 507.43 a month of study, and a dormitory bed averages about EUR 197 a month in Ljubljana. The temporary residence permit for study covers a full degree. NPR figures are rough, at EUR 1 about NPR 175.

exams: English proof for English taught programmes (one guide: IELTS 6.5; the programme page decides)
Programme specific selection by the University of Luxembourg, which teaches in English, French and German
abroad_add.intakes: September (autumn semester); non EU applications for the University of Luxembourg carry a EUR 100 fee, deducted from the first invoice if you enrol
abroad_add.work: Master and PhD students, and bachelor students after the first two semesters, may work up to 15 hours a week in term time and up to 40 hours a week in holidays; bachelor and BTS students cannot work in the first two semesters; doctoral researchers and contracted assistants are exempt (European Commission EU Immigration Portal, Luxembourg page).
abroad_add.stay_back: After finishing, a third country national may stay to look for a job or start a business and must apply for the residence permit for that purpose before the student permit ends, at least 30 days beforehand (European Commission). The page read gives no length in months.
abroad_add.note: The University of Luxembourg is the only public university. It lists enrolment fees of EUR 400 a semester for the first two bachelor semesters, EUR 200 from the third to the sixth and generally EUR 200 a semester for a master (studyeagles.com citing the university), so a bachelor starts at about EUR 800 in year one; one 2024 guide prints EUR 400 to 800 a semester for non EU students, and some specialised or private programmes cost more, so read the programme page. Living is the real cost: the university is quoted at about EUR 1,500 a month, and guides print proof of funds of EUR 950 a month excluding rent or EUR 1,100 to 1,500 a month. Public transport is free. The figure here runs from EUR 950 to EUR 1,500 a month. NPR figures are rough, at EUR 1 about NPR 175.

exams: Greek language B2 for the free Greek taught route (most international students take a one year preparatory Greek course first)
IELTS 6.0 or TOEFL iBT 79 for English taught programmes (Aristotle University medicine, one guide)
Panhellenic style admission or document review set by each university
abroad_add.intakes: Autumn semester; dates and application windows differ by university and by Greek or English route
fields: Master programmes in English (200 or more in one guide)
abroad_add.work: You can work part time during studies (European Commission EU Immigration Portal, Greece page); two 2026 guides print at least 15 hours a week, and one says a 2026 law raised the cap to 20 hours, which the Commission page does not show, so ask the university.
abroad_add.stay_back: Sources disagree. The Commission page read says you must return to your home country after your studies and apply afresh from there, while two 2026 guides (unipage.net, eecglobal.com) describe a one year post study permit to look for work (a Type H.11 permit under Law 5275/2026); confirm with the Ministry of Migration and Asylum before you rely on either.
abroad_add.note: Greek taught first cycle study at public universities is free of tuition for EU and non EU students alike, with free textbooks (unipage.net, college-council.com), but you need Greek at B2 and usually a preparatory year. English taught bachelor programmes cost about EUR 4,000 to 6,000 a year for most subjects and EUR 12,000 to 17,000 for English medicine (QS figures quoted by college-council.com; study-abroad.org prints EUR 1,500 to 7,000 and up to EUR 9,000; Aristotle University medicine is about USD 13,560), and English master programmes about EUR 1,500 to 7,000. Living is quoted at EUR 500 to 900 a month; a study visa needs proof of about USD 452 a month in one guide (about EUR 400 or more in another), and the residence permit costs about EUR 150 to 169 a year. Private universities opened under a 2024 law at about EUR 6,000 to 15,000 a year, so check Ministry accreditation. NPR figures are rough, at EUR 1 about NPR 175.

scholarship_note_add.s-quota: In 2081/82 the ministry reported NPR 5.11 billion for 10,594 students under the Medical Education Scholarship (Edusanjal and OnlineKhabar, 9 February 2025).
